title: Digitally enabled flexible implementation of medical rehabilitation for adolescents with scoliosis: a non-inferiority study
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate whether a partially digital rehabilitation program for adolescents with scoliosis is as effective as conventional inpatient rehabilitation. Eligible participants are adolescents with scoliosis who have previously completed at least one rehabilitation program. Weeks 1 and 4 of the rehabilitation will take place at the Asklepios Katharina-Schroth Clinic, while weeks 2 and 3 will be delivered digitally from the participants’ homes. The rehabilitation program will be provided via an online platform that includes individual and group sessions as well as instructional videos. 

The study will include questionnaire-based assessments, interviews, analysis of therapy diaries, workshops, and a cost analysis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The non-inferiority study includes adolescents aged 14 to 17 years (at the time of rehabilitation initiation) with scoliosis who have already completed an inpatient rehabilitation program at the Asklepios Katharina Schroth Clinic in Bad Sobernheim and whose rehabilitation is funded by one of the participating statutory pension insurance institutions.
Exclusion criteria:
Adolescents with substantial limitations in cognitive functioning, self-organization skills, or digital competencies that would impair their ability to participate are excluded. Further exclusion criteria include marked psychological distress or insufficient self-motivation. We also exclude adolescents with current or previous problematic internet or media use to prevent a potential deterioration of usage behavior.
